reason: The hypothesis directly mirrors the process, mechanism, and outcomes described in E2, which reports the same two-step oxy-nitriding at 650 °C, the discontinuous TiN layer enabling diffusion, the interconnected porous buffer layer acting as a stress absorber, and the resulting low COF and wear resistance. E1 provides general background on plasma nitriding of titanium alloys and the drawbacks of high-temperature treatments, supporting the rationale for low-temperature processing, but the specific structural and performance claims rely entirely on E2.
premises: A two-step plasma oxy-nitriding process at 650 °C with an oxygen-rich first step prevents continuous TiN formation and creates a discontinuous TiNxOy layer.
The discontinuous layer enables enhanced subsequent diffusion of N and O, forming a graded compound layer with an underlying interconnected porous buffer structure.
The porous buffer layer acts as a stress absorber, reducing stress concentration and retarding crack propagation during wear.
This specific microstructure yields a ~20% reduction in friction coefficient and improved wear performance compared to untreated TC4.
Low-temperature (650 °C) processing avoids β-phase destabilization and mechanical degradation while achieving the desired layer.
